verdict.rationale: SES documents a single SendEmail API action (API v2) supporting Simple, Raw and Templated messages, callable via AWS SDKs or directly, and a community user calls it great for transactional email. However, sending first requires verifying an identity, and sandbox accounts can only send to verified addresses, so it is not a pure one-call start. Missing for 10: copy-paste quickstart code samples, documentation of minimal required fields, evidence that a message ID is returned for tracking, and hands-on corroboration of the send flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can send a transactional email with one documented API call — minimal required fields, copy-paste quickstart code, and a message id back for tracking

citations.quote: You can use the Amazon SES API v2 to send the following types of messages: Simple ... Raw ... Templated
You can send email from Amazon EC2 by using an AWS SDK, by using the Amazon SES SMTP interface, or by making calls directly to the Amazon SES API.
SES === great for transactional emails if you handle the templating yourself.
